summary: Round 12 delta is one archive row pointer, one backlog row (M0.91), one M0.90 pointer phrase and the BUDGET_MILLIS javadoc. VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT in my own review tree (/tmp/binjava-review-trees/reviewer.qlYkmEmr, REVIEW_ROUND_BUDGET=20 exported): with b.environment().remove("REVIEW_ROUND_BUDGET") inserted in packet() immediately before the varargs loop, ./gradlew -p buildSrc test --tests binjava.ReviewRoundBudgetTest --rerun-tasks is BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 4 tests, including the sibling theBudgetIsOVERRIDABLESoItIsAPromptRatherThanAWall which puts the variable back after the remove; without it, thePacketREFUSESToOpenAnotherRoundPastTheBudget(Path) FAILED at ReviewRoundBudgetTest.java:138, 4 completed 1 failed. The round-11 major (M4.13-r11-1) is closed: M0.91's advice is correct in both the location (packet(), before the loop) and the ordering argument. The javadoc history claim also checks out: staged_tree 924876a7, the state immediately before the consolidation, holds exactly five copies in four files with four distinct values (backlog-done.md:177 14.6s, backlog-notes.md:950 17.1s, backlog.md M0.90 16.4s, CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:91 14.6s, CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:270 15.2s on 20 cores), so 'five copies in four files ... four different values' is exact where the prior 'four copies' was not. The single-home claim holds today: grepping 14-17s figures over *.md/*.java/*.sh finds them only in that javadoc (check-mutants.sh:65's 14.6s is an unrelated mutation-run figure). Both new pointer phrases are true: BUDGET_MILLIS's VALUE is 60_000 and is only printed at :289-290, never asserted, so 'not its value, which IS the budget' corrects a genuinely misleading phrase; @Timeout(value = 300) is on the class at :65, 300/15 is near 20x and 60/15 near 4x. 15.4s and 15.7s are corroborated by daemon logs (15390 ms, 15724 ms under /tmp/binjava-review-trees/gradle-home). Cost lens: the delta is docs plus one test javadoc and one comment, no object-store request path, and the sweep runs on MemoryBinStore, so no request rate scales with records, shards, partitions or indices.

findings.title: 'each figure from a named run' names one run of five, and the 14.6s attributed to this harness is the one figure I could not corroborate
findings.failure_scenario: The sentence promises attribution ('each figure from a named run') and then gives one label for four figures ('in review trees'). Corroboration on this machine: 15.1s = 15090/15146 ms, 15.2s = 15206 ms, 15.4s = 15390 ms, 15.7s = 15724 ms, all in review-tree artifacts; but the only 1,000-seed figures in THIS harness's own build output are 14723 ms and 13982 ms, i.e. 14.7s and 14.0s, with nothing at 14.6s. That is inside run-to-run variance and no threshold is derived from it (M0.90's 20x and the in-test 4x both use ~15s), so nothing is wrong today. What is weakened is the property the consolidation exists for: whoever sees 16s next cannot tell which of the five runs to compare against, because four share one label and the fifth does not match the artifact on disk. NOT WORTH A ROUND: test-results are overwritten per invocation, so the absence of a 14.6s artifact is weak evidence, and rewording this is the prose-surface churn rounds 9-11 spent themselves on. Put it in the commit body or drop it.
